Meet Maxi, robotic AI with true imagination.

Maxi runs the future before it acts. Give it a scene, let it change something, and watch what it sees, inside the physics engine that doesn't know any physics equations. Now licensable for robotics, chips and platforms.

Built from the Blueprints Ulam and von Neumann left for GAPI, based on their classified P=NP“Incidentally, the other day I developed a method that always allows a finite decision for the effective provability question concerning propositions that are built up solely by means of the concepts ‘not’, ‘or’ (thus also ‘and’, ‘follows’, etc.), [and] ‘provable’ … Perhaps, if it interests you, or you have not yet thought of it, then I can write it up.”John von Neumann to Kurt Gödel, Berlin, 12 January 1931. Collected Works vol. V, pp. 340–341. Provenance link to follow. and intractable quantum computing“Let me point to the so-called Monte Carlo approach as an example of one of the methods that can lead to insight into the behavior of complicated systems. Essentially it consists of imitating physical processes on a computer by following a large but manageable number, replacing the trillions or more that are involved in the real process, by thousands of histories of the behavior of individual particles.”Stanislaw Ulam, Science, Computers, and People, pp. 38–39. And Martin Gardner's preface, p. viii: “the Monte Carlo method of solving intractable problems, not only in probability theory but in areas such as number theory where the method would not have been thought applicable.” Provenance links to follow. work, developed at Los Alamos while working on the Super hydrogen-bomb project. This is not a world model.

A million hours of video, or three centuries of equations, compressed into weights or formulas and evaluated forward. Reconstructive compression, the same trick an LLM does with text. They describe what happened well and predict what happens next badly. Move an object and the policy collapses.

No corpus, no equations. Give the engine a world and run it; light, heat, contact and gravity emerge from the run. Catching a frisbee is not retrieval; it is running the disc forward and moving to where it will be. Nothing to look up, only something to run.

Every edit is a declared intervention, so the record tracks what was done, not just what is.
Maxi doesn't guess what changed. It changed it.

Runs the edited world forward and watches it. Its first instrument is its eyes: it records video of what it is imagining and flies drone-like flybys through the scene to see it from wherever it needs to. Raw data, clocks and stills come second, as they do for a person.
What if I move this? Maxi runs it and looks.
Watches what it recorded against what it expected.
Infers a scene program from what it saw. It records the counterfactuals that worked and conjectures new ones from what it learned before, and it can branch a world at any tick.
Maxi learns by imagining. The rules it recovers are executable, and the next imagination starts from them.

See it think. At egpt-godsworld.descix.net you talk to Maxi on one side of the screen and watch its imagination on the other. Say “put light in the scene and let light do what light does” and see what it sees.
Optics, circuits and mechanics are three vocabularies over the same engine. A grasp, a beam and a wire are the same operators. A model that learns light has learned contact.
Fidelity is a dial, not a rewrite.
Cheap idealised collisions for geometry; full inter-particle collisions where friction matters. Maxi picks the physics it is imagining.
“Where will the rings form at these settings” is auto-scorable, so Maxi improves without a human labelling anything.
Each scene opens live in the engine. Click one and watch it compute in your own tab.

Nothing here is a recording. Each scene is computed in your tab by an engine that doesn't know any physics equations, and it either shows up or it doesn't. The same engine runs on an iPhone with the network off, simulating the double slit in 3D.

Hardware quantum computers, still years away, hope to simulate a hundred particles. FRQTL simulates billions on off-the-shelf chips, today, and the mathematics of why it works is machine-checked and published.

FRQTL is the FRame And QuanTum Language virtual machine: physics computed by combinatorics and fractal recursion instead of calculus, quantum “balls” in gravitational frame “boxes.” It exceeds what a superposition-based quantum computer could do in theory, on classical hardware, in your browser.

Behind it is a proof of P = NP, formalised in Lean 4 in three independent chains. Two of them use only Lean's two structural axioms, propext and Quot.sound: no sorryAx, no Classical.choice. A choice-free proof is constructive: it does not just say a solution exists, it is the algorithm that finds it.

This proof boils down to the following three claims:

axiom Electrons_On_Circuits_Is_Physical_SAT
axiom RET_Reduction_PhysicsEntropy_to_ShannonEntropy
axiom ShannonEntropyInPbyShannonCoding

“Certainly, it follows from these three assumptions that P = NP. I don't know what are the shannon entropy problem and the physical system entropy problem, but the result here suggests that you should really dig into these because at least one of these assumptions is probably faulty.”
Mario Carneiro, Lean maintainer, on the first draft of the proof. The entailment conceded, the doubt located in three axioms. The three chains above are those axioms, discharged.

The most publicly and rigorously substantiated quantum and computing breakthrough there is: the impossible calculations run in your browser, and the proofs of why they run are published for anyone to check.

The physics engine that doesn't know any physics equations. Discrete fractal physics, integer rules, Rust compiled to WASM. Efficient enough to run the 3D double slit on an iPhone, offline. Same binary in the browser and headless in Node. For game-engine developers: a sprite is a quantum, a layer is a dimension, a tick is a tick.
Developer alpha of the SDK: after the preview, and it earns DAITA.
Bit-exact real and transcendental arithmetic in place of floating point. Matrices, polynomials, order-finding and transcendental functions on exact values, so error never accumulates.
Drag-and-drop desktop physics. Emitters, walls, tunnels, detector walls and logic gates on a palette; a live 2D/3D canvas; layers and an inspector; every project is also code.
A visual flow canvas for building codecs on exact arithmetic, with the code drawer always in sync. Drop a transform, see the chain; edit the code, see the chain rebuild.

Mathematica meets cellular automata, named with a nod to Lean. .frqnb notebooks with math, canvas, chart, view and module cells; the canvas cell is a live simulation. Same files in the browser and in VS Code.

Which one do you need? Robotics and embodied-AI teams license Maxi. Chip and hardware makers start with FRQTL and the FAT tier. Simulation teams take STUDIO and the engine. Codec and signal-processing teams take ROSETTA and EGPT Math. Research groups start in FAT.

Outside it, Courant Group sells commercial-grade licences and sends at least a tenth of the revenue, half in year one, back through the DeSciX treasury to buy the token contributors hold. Each turn makes the engine better and the token scarcer.

A physics engine nobody can read is a physics engine nobody trusts. Approved developers inside DeSciX read the source, run the builds, and improve them; that is where the science gets done and where it gets checked.

Commercial products need optimised, supported, commercial-grade builds, hardware integration, and terms that respect export controls and exclusivity. That is what Courant Group sells, and it is the only thing it sells.

Academic economics pay for publishing. This wheel pays for understanding: the people who make Maxi imagine better are paid in the asset that commercial use buys back. The incentive and the outcome point the same way.

In 1952 the Atomic Energy Commission put an electronic computer at NYU's Courant Institute. Von Neumann, then an AEC commissioner, had corresponded with Courant for decades about computing shocks with difference equations: the continuous world, handled by discrete steps.

In 1951 a star undergraduate of Alonzo Church's named Gian-Carlo Rota was at Princeton, with von Neumann lurking in Fine Hall. A few years later, in 1956, that same young man, now a newly minted Yale PhD, arrived at Courant as a postdoc. Von Neumann died the next year with his new science unpublished. Rota spent the rest of his life at Los Alamos and MIT carrying what Ulam and von Neumann had started, and in 1991 he handed it to a student.

Courant Group is named for the room where continuous physics met discrete computation, and for the year the work went underground. Maxi is that work, finished: a physics engine that doesn't know any physics equations, and a mind that imagines in it.

Licences are paid in EGPT, not dollars. That is the engine of the flywheel: to license Maxi you hold the community's token, and the price scales with the tokens in circulation.

Anyone can run the engines: the compiled builds are public. The source is open to approved developers inside DeSciX, behind a KYC gate that complies with domicile regulations, including export controls.
The public builds are for learning and experimenting; they are not optimised and not commercial grade. Commercial-grade builds come with a licence.

A licence is acquired with EGPT. Ten enterprise licences, priced in order of signing, from ten million tokens for the first to a hundred million for the last. No equity. Each negotiated individually; exclusivity by geography or industry available; subject to US export controls.
Licences are not perpetual. The initial term is five years, renewable. A minimum of 10 percent of licence proceeds, 50 percent in year one, returns to the community through the DeSciX treasury.

The roles are the delegated-proof-of-stake roles of the DAITA token economy: stakeholders, witness-validators, node operators, developers, delegates, a treasury, referrers and resellers. An enterprise licence is held within one of them; the role sets what the licence covers, the tier sets the price.
A living experiment, with EGPT as the test case.

The economic model is a living and evolving experiment, and EGPT, the token needed to license Maxi and FRQTL, is its test case. The controlling real-world contract is the DeSciX Community License Membership Agreement; read it, it is not summarised here. The whitepapers it references are its conceptual inspiration: DAITA: A Sustainable Data Economy for Artificial Intelligence for the token economy, its roles and its market protocols, and the DeSciX whitepaper for community source and the IP-IPO.
